subject: maths
title: Volume of 3D Shapes
welcome_lead: Step into 3 dimensions. Cubes, cuboids, and cylinders all have space inside — let's measure it.
meta_desc: Calculate volumes of cubes, cuboids and cylinders in this KS3 geometry adventure.
final_note: Fantastic! You can now measure 3D space confidently.

concepts.def: The amount of 3D space a solid takes up.
A 3D shape with 6 equal square faces.
A 3D shape with two circular ends.
Units for volume, such as cm³ or m³.
A 2D shape made by slicing through a solid.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Volume = side × side × side = s³.

For a cube with side 4 cm: V = 4 × 4 × 4 = 64 cm³.

Volume = length × width × height.

For a cuboid 5 × 3 × 2 cm: V = 5 × 3 × 2 = 30 cm³.

Volume = π × r² × h (area of circle × height).

For radius 2 cm, height 5 cm: V = π × 4 × 5 = 20π ≈ 62.83 cm³.
